content.comment_body: Is it possible to use this temperature sensor as a 0-10V input for [product_name] 24RCE? Can the LM35DZ replace [product_name] pt100 and RTD modules in budget-friendly projects?

You can technically connect this sensor to the [product_name], but without a high-quality analog amplifier, it is not practical. The sensor's output is 0mV + 10mV/°C, so for typical room temperatures ranging from 0°C to 50°C, the voltage will only be between 0V and 0.5V. This results in poor resolution when used with [product_name]. Alternatively, a circuit providing 4-20mA output might help, but you should first assess the resolution of [product_name]. Analog inputs with a range of 0 to 10V produce values from 0 to 1000; using only a 0 to 1V input means you only get values from 0 to 100. [product_name]'s accuracy is around 1.5%, or about 15 units out of 1000. With a reading of 100 (from 1V), the margin is ±15, translating to roughly ±15% error. For example, with a temperature reading of 100°C at 1V (value 100), the actual value could be anywhere from 85°C to 115°C. Regards, [user_name]
No, that is not possible. The basic [product_name] does not have analog inputs.

analysis.insight_summary: Community members considered using an LM35DZ temperature sensor as a 0-10V input for [product_name] systems instead of higher-cost sensor modules. Feedback discussed practical constraints, including limited voltage range and analog input resolution on [product_name], as well as overall compatibility issues. These factors hinder the sensor’s reliability and usefulness in this configuration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to use the LM35DZ sensor as a more affordable solution for analog temperature measurement, expecting it to replace pricier traditional sensor modules in the [product_name] platform and provide similar performance.
